newsitem.title: USA: Rexworks to sell assets, rest of company.
newsitem.headline: Rexworks to sell assets, rest of company.

text.p: Rexworks Inc said Monday it had agreed to two separate deals under which it would sell certain assets of its compactor and grinder business and then all of its common stock.
Rexworks said it expects net proceeds from the two transactions, which are projected to occur simultaneously, of $5.00 to $5.25 a share after expenses.
Proceeds would be distributed to shareholders, it said.

Rexworks said it entered into a letter of intent with CMI Corp for CMI to acquire certain assets related to Rexworks' compactor and material reduction grinder business segments. This transaction is subject to several factors including negotiation of a definitive agreement as well as shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Rexworks said it also entered into a definitive agreement, subsequent to the sale of the compactor and grinder assets, to sell all its outstanding common stock to Giuffre Bros. Cranes Inc of Milwaukee, Wis. This transaction is also subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.
Rexworks said it expects the transactions to close about November 30.

In a separate statement, Oklahoma City-based CMI, which makes automated road building equipment, said the two product lines it plans to acquire from Rexworks contributed about $30 million in revenue in fiscal 1996.

CMI also said it expects these product lines to be profitable in their first full year despite the costs of moving the production to Oklahoma City. The purchase price and terms of the proposed acquisition were not disclosed.

"These product lines are precisely the sort of strategic acquisition we are seeking," Bill Swisher, chairman, said in a statement. "Each business fits our core competencies like a glove. Each involves similar components and fabrication techniques; and each serves related customers and markets to our existing businesses, thereby delivering seamless, vertical integration from a marketing, manufacturing and engineering standpoint."
He said efficiencies resulting from this acquisition should increase CMI's gross margins, making them compare favorably with its other products.
